stories.title: Record the v2 architecture and bounded contexts
acceptance: The architecture names identity, catalog, publishing, artifacts, moderation, payments, entitlements, analytics, and operations as separate modules.
Release A and Release B exclusions are explicit.

stories.title: Define typed environment contracts
acceptance: Production refuses placeholder secrets, loopback dependency URLs, mismatched clusters, and missing required settings.
Frontend and backend expose one documented environment contract.

stories.title: Create the v2 design-system foundation
acceptance: Semantic tokens cover color, type, spacing, radii, motion, focus, and status states.
Primitives meet keyboard, focus, contrast, loading, and disabled-state requirements.

stories.title: Install the automated quality harness
acceptance: CI runs frontend unit, API integration, migration, E2E smoke, accessibility, dependency, and container checks.
A failing check blocks merge.

stories.title: Pass the foundation gate
acceptance: Configuration, design-system, and CI contracts pass together on a clean checkout.

stories.title: Create atomic session and nonce persistence
acceptance: Nonces are single-use and sessions rotate atomically under concurrent refresh.
Session revocation invalidates access and refresh paths.

stories.title: Implement standards-based Solana sign-in
acceptance: The server verifies exact domain, URI, address, chain, nonce, issued-at, expiry, message bytes, and signature.
Legacy signMessage remains a tested fallback.

stories.title: Replace wallet-adapter UX with Wallet Standard sign-in
acceptance: Wallet connection and application sign-in are separate, explicit states.
The dialog explains that sign-in is free and displays domain and network.

stories.title: Add shared authentication abuse controls
acceptance: Route decorators work in the required order and limits use Redis across API workers.
Forwarded client IPs are trusted only from the edge proxy.

stories.title: Build approved-creator onboarding
acceptance: A creator supplies a unique handle, display name, bio, support link, terms acceptance, and payout address.
Only approved creators can create drafts.

stories.title: Pass the identity gate
acceptance: Desktop and mobile users can sign in, restore, rotate, list, and revoke sessions without console errors.

stories.title: Create the v2 catalog state model
acceptance: Creator, listing, and release states have constrained transitions and audit records.
Drafts cannot appear in public queries.

stories.title: Enforce listing validation contracts
acceptance: The API constrains content lengths, URLs, prices, licenses, categories, and listing-type fields.
Invalid and duplicate submissions return stable error codes.

stories.title: Build the creator studio shell
acceptance: Studio navigation covers overview, drafts, published listings, releases, analytics, and settings.
Unauthorized users receive an intentional sign-in or onboarding state.

stories.title: Replace immediate publishing with a draft editor
acceptance: Creation saves a private draft and never publishes directly.
The editor supports autosave, validation, preview, and explicit review submission.

stories.title: Implement moderation queues and decisions
acceptance: Moderators approve, reject, suspend, and restore creators, listings, and releases with reasons.
Every decision produces an immutable audit event.

stories.title: Add abuse reports and legal surfaces
acceptance: Users can report public entities and track a report receipt.
Terms, Privacy, Acceptable Use, Security, and contact links appear on every public page.

stories.title: Pass the catalog and moderation gate
acceptance: Unapproved content cannot enter public results and suspended content disappears without evidence loss.

stories.title: Create release manifests and immutable versions
acceptance: Every release records semantic version, digest, size, type, license, compatibility, permissions, support, and install metadata.
Published release records are immutable.

stories.title: Implement private object storage and signed uploads
acceptance: Creators upload through short-lived scoped URLs and cannot choose arbitrary storage keys.
Size, media type, and digest are verified server-side.

stories.title: Build quarantine and artifact scanning
acceptance: New artifacts remain quarantined until malware and policy scans pass.
Failed scans block review and expose a stable creator-facing reason.

stories.title: Implement entitlement-bound delivery and install events
acceptance: Downloads use short-lived URLs bound to user, release, and entitlement.
Install analytics derive from deduplicated audit events.

stories.title: Build release and installation UX
acceptance: Creators can submit an artifact and manifest with a visible scan state.
Buyers can acquire a free release, view permissions, download it, and reopen instructions from the library.

stories.title: Pass the artifact gate
acceptance: A reviewed free listing completes upload, scan, publication, acquisition, download, and reinstall without manual database work.

stories.title: Replace promotional claims with measured product truth
acceptance: The home page displays live time-bounded metrics or no metric.
Navigation contains Marketplace, Publish, Documentation, and wallet/session controls.

stories.title: Redesign marketplace discovery
acceptance: Filters synchronize with the URL and support accessible loading, empty, and error states.
Cards show creator, version, compatibility, scan status, license, and measured installs.

stories.title: Redesign listing detail around trust and installation
acceptance: The screen answers what it does, who made it, what it accesses, where it runs, how it installs, and why it is trusted before showing acquisition.
Suspended or incompatible releases cannot be acquired.

stories.title: Complete saves, library, and verified reviews
acceptance: Only entitled buyers can review and creators cannot review their own listings.
Saved and acquired listings have distinct, functional surfaces.

stories.title: Pass accessibility, responsive, and performance budgets
acceptance: Primary journeys meet WCAG 2.2 AA at 320, 768, 1024, and 1440 pixels.
Production mobile p75 LCP target is below 2.5 seconds and wallet controls cause no layout shift.

stories.title: Pass the curated free beta gate
acceptance: All Release A PRD gates have current evidence and at least ten reviewed listings from three approved creators are installable.

stories.title: Specify the USDC payment state machine and threat model
acceptance: States, transitions, invariants, accounts, fee split, finality, expiry, retries, refunds, and operator actions are explicit.
The threat model covers replay, intent hijack, wrong mint, wrong recipient, partial payment, overpayment, RPC disagreement, and concurrency.

stories.title: Create constrained payment persistence
acceptance: Database constraints enforce unique signatures, idempotency, valid amounts, valid transitions, and one active entitlement per user/listing/release.
All monetary fields use integer token base units.

stories.title: Implement payment-intent APIs
acceptance: Intent creation freezes the complete expected transaction and honors an idempotency key.
Submission is buyer-bound, atomic, monotonic, and queues verification once.

stories.title: Build the USDC checkout transaction
acceptance: Checkout displays network, mint, amount, seller, platform fee, total, expiry, and irreversible-payment notice.
The transaction matches the server intent and supports wallet rejection, expiry, pending, finalized, and retry states.

stories.title: Implement asynchronous semantic chain verification
acceptance: The worker verifies signer, cluster, finality, token program, mint, source owner, exact base-unit amounts, recipients, fee split, memo/reference, and transaction success.
RPC null, timeout, lag, and disagreement remain retryable until explicit expiry.

stories.title: Project verified payments into entitlements and receipts
acceptance: Only a finalized verifier result grants a paid entitlement.
The buyer receives a stable receipt with transaction, release, amount, fee, and entitlement status.

stories.title: Build reconciliation and recovery tools
acceptance: Operators can inspect, replay, expire, and reconcile intents without direct database edits.
Entitlements can be rebuilt idempotently from verified records.

stories.title: Pass the paid-mainnet security gate
acceptance: One hundred devnet purchases, replay tests, chaos tests, a 24-hour soak, and independent review pass without unresolved P0 or P1 findings.

stories.title: Create the production service topology
acceptance: Web, API, PostgreSQL, Redis, chain worker, and scan worker use health checks and private networks.
Only the edge proxy exposes public ports.

stories.title: Harden TLS, headers, secrets, and host access
acceptance: One approved edge proxy terminates TLS; the insecure Traefik dashboard and permissive CSP are removed.
Production has no default secrets, public databases, password SSH, or unneeded firewall ports.

stories.title: Automate migrations, backups, restore, and rollback
acceptance: Deploys stop on migration mismatch and run an explicit migration job.
Encrypted off-site backup, clean restore, and application rollback are demonstrated.

stories.title: Add production observability and dependency health
acceptance: Liveness and readiness are separate and readiness checks database, Redis, and required workers.
Alerts cover error rate, auth abuse, queue lag, RPC health, payment failures, scan failures, disk, memory, backup age, and certificate expiry.

stories.title: Build gated CI/CD with staging promotion
acceptance: CI builds immutable images, produces an SBOM, scans dependencies and containers, deploys staging, runs smoke tests, and requires approval for production.
Failed health checks trigger documented rollback.

stories.title: Run the production-like staging soak
acceptance: Staging runs for 24 hours with synthetic browsing, publishing, scanning, installation, and devnet payment traffic.
All injected dependency failures produce alerts and recover without data drift.

stories.title: Execute controlled production rollout
acceptance: Release A opens to invited users with monitoring, backups, support, and rollback staffed.
Release B stays disabled until PAY-008 passes and receives separate operator approval.
